# sightline Eyes and a stopwatch for AI coding agents on Windows. One small exe, command `sight`. sightline finds windows, screenshots them even when covered, waits for the UI to change and then stop changing, and tells the agent how image pixels map to screen, window and client coordinates. It also measures CPU and memory of a whole process tree. It **only observes**: it never clicks, types or moves the mouse. The agent acts with its own tools, then uses sightline to check the result. [Why](#why-sightline) • [Install](#install) • [Quick start](#quick-start) • [Use with agents](#use-it-with-ai-agents) • [Reference](docs/REFERENCE.md) • [FAQ](#faq) ``` sight list --exe notepad # which window? sight shot --hwnd 15603054 --settle 300 # what does it look like, once it is stable? sight wait --hwnd 15603054 --change --settle 300 # after my click: has the UI changed and settled? sight stat --pid 19668 --duration 2000 # how much CPU and RAM? ``` ## Why sightline Asked to "check the dialog looks right", an agent on Windows usually writes a throwaway PowerShell script: `Start-Sleep 3`, `CopyFromScreen`, a hard-coded PID. sightline replaces that. | The throwaway script | What goes wrong | sightline | |---|---|---| | `Start-Sleep 3` | Too short is flaky, too long is slow | `--settle 300` waits until pixels stop changing, with a timeout and an honest `settled:false` | | `Start-Sleep 0.5` after a click | The UI may not have started changing yet, so a plain settle returns the old frame | `--expect-change` waits for pixels to differ from a baseline first, then settles | | `CopyFromScreen` | Whatever is on top ends up in the image | `shot --hwnd` captures the window itself, even when covered | | Window capture APIs | Right-click menus are separate windows and get missed | The app's own popups are detected and included | | The model resizes the image | Pixel positions no longer match the screen | Every shot returns a `formula` from image px to screen px | | Hand-cut `Crop`, window moved to a fixed spot first | Breaks when the window is somewhere else | `--crop x,y,w,h` is window-relative and position-independent; `formula_window` and `formula_client` map pixels to window and client coordinates | | 150% DPI scaling | Hand-made coordinate math breaks | Per-Monitor DPI aware; reports `dpi_scale` and `monitor_dpi_scale` | | `Get-Process` | One process, hard-coded PID | `list` finds the PID; `stat` covers the whole tree with avg / p95 / max | | Free-form text | The agent parses prose and guesses what failed | One JSON line, stable error codes, and a `hint` naming the next step | Images are written to a file and only the **path** is returned, never base64, so a screenshot costs one file read instead of thousands of tokens. ## Commands | Command | Answers | Notes | |---|---|---| | `list` | Which windows exist, and which PID / HWND do I target? | Rect, monitor, DPI, minimized state; noisy windows hidden by default | | `shot` | What does this window look like now? | Covered windows, popups, change and settle wait, window-relative `--crop`, coordinate formulas | | `wait` | Has the UI changed and settled after my action? | Same waiting as `shot`, no image; `changed`, `change_ms`, `settled` | | `rec` | Show me what happened: an animated GIF | Window, crop or region to GIF; merges identical frames; `--until-settled`, `--keyframes` stills | | `stat` | How much CPU and RAM over time? | Whole process tree (Electron, browsers, games); private bytes | | `doctor` | What monitors and DPI scales does this machine have? | First stop when something looks off | ## Install **PowerShell one-liner** (installs to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\sight` and adds it to your user `PATH`): ```powershell irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sao-coding/sightline/main/install.ps1 | iex ``` Open a **new terminal** afterwards so the `PATH` change is picked up, then check with `sight doctor`. Pin a version, change the folder, or uninstall: ```powershell $env:SIGHT_VERSION = "0.1.0"; irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sao-coding/sightline/main/install.ps1 | iex $env:SIGHT_INSTALL_DIR = 'D:\tools\sight'; irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sao-coding/sightline/main/install.ps1 | iex $env:SIGHT_UNINSTALL = 1; irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sao-coding/sightline/main/install.ps1 | iex ``` The script verifies the download against the `sight.exe.sha256` published with each release. **Manual.** Download `sight.exe` from [Releases](../../releases) (`sight-windows-x64.zip` also holds the docs and the skill), put it in a folder, and add that folder to `PATH`: ```powershell # example: C:\tools\sight (user PATH, no admin needed) [Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable('Path', "$([Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable('Path','User'));C:\tools\sight", 'User') ``` Or via Settings → System → About → Advanced system settings → Environment Variables → `Path` → New. Restart the terminal (and the agent) afterwards. Agents must be able to find `sight` on their `PATH`. **From source** (Windows 10/11, Rust toolchain): ```powershell cargo build --release # target\release\sight.exe ``` ## Quick start ``` sight doctor # monitors and DPI sight list --exe notepad # find the target sight shot --hwnd 15603054 --settle 300 # capture it once stable ``` One turn of the agent loop: 1. **Find the target.** ``` > sight list --exe notepad {"v":1,"ok":true,"data":{"count":1,"windows":[{"hwnd":15603054,"pid":19668,"exe":"Notepad.exe","title":"Untitled - Notepad","rect":{"x":3010,"y":362,"w":1178,"h":637},"monitor":1,"dpi_scale":1.0,"monitor_dpi_scale":1.0,"minimized":false}]},"warnings":[]} ``` 2. **Look.** Open `data.path` with the agent's image viewer. ``` > sight shot --hwnd 15603054 --settle 300 {"v":1,"ok":true,"data":{"path":"C:\\Users\\me\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\sightline\\shot-20261123-214402-405.jpg","image":{"w":1178,"h":637},"maps_to":{"space":"screen_physical","x":3010,"y":362,"w":1178,"h":637},"scale":1.0,"formula":"screen_x = 3010 + px / 1.0; screen_y = 362 + py / 1.0","settled":true,"elapsed_ms":945,"popups":[]},"warnings":[]} ``` 3. **Act** with the agent's own input tool, at coordinates computed from the formulas below. 4. **Wait for the UI**, then look. Right after an external click the UI may not have started changing, so a plain `--settle` could return the old frame. `--expect-change` (or `wait --change`) first waits for pixels to differ from a baseline, then settles. Both phases share `--timeout`: ``` > sight wait --hwnd 15603054 --change --settle 300 {"v":1,"ok":true,"data":{"changed":true,"change_ms":326,"settled":true,"elapsed_ms":492},"warnings":[]} > sight shot --hwnd 15603054 --expect-change --settle 300 # same wait, then saves the image ``` If nothing changes before the timeout, `shot` still saves the latest frame and both commands fail with `TIMEOUT` (exit 5) and `data.changed:false`. Tiny noise such as a blinking caret does not count: a change needs `--min-change-px` differing pixels (default 16). The baseline is the first captured frame, which arrives about 0.3 s after `sight` starts, so a change that already finished by then is not seen (`TIMEOUT`, `changed:false`: take a plain `shot` and look). **Instant reactions: `--baseline`.** Take a shot *before* acting and wait against it, so a change that finishes before `sight` even starts is still detected: ``` > sight shot --hwnd 15603054 --out before.png # act with your own tool; the UI reacts instantly > sight wait --hwnd 15603054 --baseline before.png --settle 300 {"v":1,"ok":true,"data":{"changed":true,"change_ms":318,"settled":true,"elapsed_ms":502},"warnings":[]} ``` The same order with `wait --change` and no `--baseline` fails with a false `TIMEOUT`. Each shot writes a sidecar `before.sight.json`; a baseline from another window, with another `--crop`, or of another kind (window vs region) is `INVALID_ARGS`, never a silent wrong comparison. A window that was resized or expanded since the baseline counts as a change (`changed:true`, warning `baseline_size_changed`). 5. **Re-check** with the same `shot` and compare. For performance, run `stat` while the app works: ``` > sight stat --pid 17400 --duration 2000 {"v":1,"ok":true,"data":{"pid":17400,"exe":"powershell.exe","duration_ms":2038,"samples":4,"logical_cores":16,"cpu_core_pct":{"avg":100.42,"p95":104.98,"max":104.98},"cpu_total_pct":{"avg":6.28,"p95":6.56,"max":6.56},"mem_mb":{"avg":52.87,"p95":52.87,"max":52.87},"processes":[...]},"warnings":[]} ``` One full core (`cpu_core_pct` ≈ 100) out of 16 (`cpu_total_pct` ≈ 6.3): a busy loop. ### Recording a GIF `sight rec` records a window or region for README demos and test evidence. It blocks until it is done, so run it in the background while you act: ```powershell $job = Start-Job { sight rec --hwnd 123456 --duration 10000 --until-settled 500 --keyframes 3 --out C:\tmp\demo.gif } Start-Sleep -Milliseconds 700 # capture needs ~0.3 s to start # ... act with your own tool (click, type) ... $rec = Receive-Job $job -Wait -AutoRemoveJob | ConvertFrom-Json # data.path, data.keyframes[].path ``` The result has `frames`, `fps`, `duration_ms`, `size_bytes` and the same coordinate formulas as `shot`. Identical frames are merged (a static window is one long frame), and `--keyframes 3` also saves PNG stills of the biggest changes so an agent can check the recording without decoding the GIF. Defaults: `--fps 10` (max 30), `--max-edge 800`. `rec` picks one capture source when it starts and never switches: `--source auto` (default) uses screen capture of the window's rect, which includes menus, tooltips and popups, unless another window covers the target, and then window capture (`source`, `source_reason` and the warning `rec_window_source_no_popups` say which). `--pad 40` also records 40 px around the window so a dropdown that sticks out is included. The capture follows a window that moves; windows covering it mid-recording are listed in `occlusion_events`. ### Coordinates: pick the origin your input tool uses For a window shot, `shot` returns one formula per origin. Use the one that matches the origin of your own input tool, with `px, py` in the saved image: ``` > sight shot --hwnd 11736012 --crop 100,120,300,200 --max-edge 0 {"v":1,"ok":true,"data":{"image":{"w":300,"h":200},"maps_to":{"space":"screen_physical","x":307,"y":270,"w":300,"h":200},"scale":1.0,"formula":"screen_x = 307 + px / 1.0; screen_y = 270 + py / 1.0","window":{"frame":{"x":207,"y":150,"w":642,"h":452},"client":{"x":208,"y":181,"w":640,"h":420},"client_offset":{"x":1,"y":31}},"formula_window":"win_x = 100 + px / 1.0; win_y = 120 + py / 1.0","formula_client":"client_x = 99 + px / 1.0; client_y = 89 + py / 1.0","settled":true,"changed":false,"change_ms":null,"elapsed_ms":351,"popups":[]},"warnings":[]} ``` | Field | Origin | Use it for | |---|---|---| | `formula` | the screen (virtual desktop), physical px | tools that click at absolute screen coordinates | | `formula_window` | top-left of the window's DWM frame | tools relative to the window; same origin as `--crop` | | `formula_client` | top-left of the client area, below the title bar | tools relative to the client area | `window.frame` and `window.client` are in screen px; `client_offset` is the client top-left minus the frame top-left. Image point (50, 40) above is screen (357, 310), window (150, 160), client (149, 129). `--crop x,y,w,h` is relative to the window frame, so it selects the same part of the window wherever the window is. It is applied before `--scale` and `--max-edge`; `--max-edge 0` disables downscaling, so `--crop ... --max-edge 0` is exactly w×h pixels. It works with `--hwnd` and `--pid` (not `--region`), and `wait` accepts it too. ## Use it with AI agents - **[AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md)** is a one-page brief: commands, the observe loop, the coordinate formula, and what to do for each error code. Codex, Cursor and others read it automatically in this repo; copy it, or link to it, from your own project's instructions. - **`skills/sightline/SKILL.md`** is the same guidance as an Agent Skill, loaded only when needed. For Claude Code: ``` xcopy /E /I skills\sightline %USERPROFILE%\.claude\skills\sightline ``` Make sure `sight` is on the agent's `PATH` (see [Install](#install)). ## Reference Full flags and output fields for every command, the coordinate and DPI rules, popup handling, the output contract and the error codes are in **[docs/REFERENCE.md](docs/REFERENCE.md)**. ## FAQ **Which Windows versions work?** Windows 10 and 11. **Does anything leave my machine?** No. There is no network code; images stay in a local file. **Why don't `stat` numbers match Task Manager?** Memory is *private bytes* (commit), not Task Manager's "private working set". ## Building from source ```powershell cargo build --release --locked cargo test ``` ## Limitations - `--expect-change` / `wait --change` baseline on the first captured frame (about 0.3 s after start), so a change that finished earlier is not detected; use `--baseline` for that. - The window formulas and `--crop` were only verified on 100% DPI monitors; they are plain physical-px arithmetic, but not tested at 125% or 150%. - `WINDOW_PROTECTED` is untested against a real capture-protected window. - Classic Win32 `#32768` menus are untested, so their popup fallback is unverified. - The PID-reuse check uses process start time at 1-second resolution, so a PID reused within the same second is not detected. ## License [AGPL-3.0](LICENSE).

Anthropic 研究员 Nicholas Carlini 让 16 个 Claude Agent 在共享代码库里从头写 C 编译器。许多编译测试可以单独分派，但构建整个 Linux 内核时，多个 Agent 会撞到同一个缺陷，随后彼此覆盖修复。并发进程越多，仍然只有同一个故障信号。

+ +

Anthropic researcher Nicholas Carlini had 16 Claude agents write a C compiler in a shared repository. Individual compiler tests could be distributed, but when the agents built the whole Linux kernel, they ran into the same defect and overwrote each other’s fixes. More processes still shared a single failure signal.

+ +

Carlini 修改了验证程序，用 GCC 编译内核的大部分文件，交给新编译器的只是一部分。构建失败时可缩小这一部分，逐步隔离出不同文件里的问题，让 Agent 并行修。后来还需要找出单独编译能通过、组合起来却失败的文件。

+ +

Carlini changed the verifier to compile most of the kernel with GCC and hand a subset to the new compiler. Shrinking a failing subset isolated defects in different files, giving the agents independent work. He later had to find combinations of files that failed together despite passing individually.

+ +

Carlini 报告称，实验花费约 2 万美元 API 成本，经历近 2,000 次 Claude Code 会话，产出的编译器可以构建 Linux 6.9。他同时记录了仍需 GCC 处理 16 位 x86 启动代码，以及汇编器、链接器的局限。本站依据他的原始记录，未复跑编译实验。可借鉴的决策是先让共用的失败信号变成能独立定位的子问题。

+ +

Carlini reports roughly $20,000 in API costs and nearly 2,000 Claude Code sessions for a compiler that could build Linux 6.9. He also records its continued use of GCC for 16-bit x86 startup code and limitations around assembly and linking. This story draws on his account. Codex Venture did not rerun the compiler experiment. The transferable decision was to turn a shared failure signal into independently diagnosable problems.

OpenAI 的 Ryan Lopopolo 回顾了一个用 Codex 开发内部产品的工程项目。团队发现，聊天里达成共识的架构决定，如果没有进入仓库，后续的 Agent 会话就很难找到。最初试图把全部说明集中在一份 AGENTS.md 里，文档越长，越难维护，也越难判断哪些条目已经过时。

+ +

OpenAI’s Ryan Lopopolo described an internal product built with Codex. Architectural decisions made in chat were hard for later agent sessions to retrieve if they never reached the repository. An early attempt to put everything in AGENTS.md produced a growing document that was difficult to maintain and audit for stale guidance.

+ +

团队后来把根级说明当作入口，把设计、架构和实施计划放进有结构的文档目录，辅以自动检查。他还记录了人手每周清理生成代码难以持续，团队随之把部分偏好写成可以检测的规则，再安排定期任务提交有针对性的改动。

+ +

The team turned the root instructions into an entry point, moved designs, architecture, and implementation plans into structured documents, and backed them with automated checks. Lopopolo also recounts how weekly manual cleanup became hard to sustain. The team encoded some preferences as checkable rules and scheduled jobs to propose focused changes.

+ +

这是该团队的工程复盘。原作者把多年尺度的架构一致性列为仍待观察的问题。小团队可以先从一条常被漏掉、后果可检查的约束入手，为它补上仓库里的说明和自动检查，让下一次改动能直接看到反馈。

+ +

This is the team’s engineering retrospective. Lopopolo leaves architectural coherence over a period of years as an open question. A small team can start with one repeatedly missed rule whose consequences are observable, then add repository guidance and an automated check that gives feedback on the next change.

排查静态站搜索时，可以先确认构建器识别到了预期语言。准备两份 HTML，分别设置 html lang 为 en 和 zh-CN，并将可检索内容放进带 data-pagefind-body 的 main 元素。把样本放进临时目录，使试验和正式站的索引互不覆盖。

+ +

When debugging static search, start by checking that the indexer detected the expected languages. Create two HTML files with lang set to en and zh-CN, and put searchable content in a main element marked with data-pagefind-body. Use a temporary directory to keep the fixture and production indexes apart.

+ +

本站在 Darwin arm64 上使用站点锁定的 Pagefind 1.6.0，在临时目录运行 pagefind --site .。命令退出码为 0，输出包含 Discovered 2 languages: en, zh-cn 和 Indexed 2 pages。我们再从 pagefind/pagefind-entry.json 核对了两个语言键。

+ +

On Darwin arm64 we ran the site’s locked Pagefind 1.6.0 with pagefind --site . in a temporary directory. It exited with code 0 and printed “Discovered 2 languages: en, zh-cn” and “Indexed 2 pages.” We checked both language keys in pagefind/pagefind-entry.json.

+ +

如果只生成一个语言键，先检查两份输入 HTML 的 html lang 和构建目录。这个样本采用每页一种声明语言，适合检查索引覆盖。中英文在同一 URL 内的查询行为和分词相关性，需要用实际站点的搜索结果确认。

+ +

If only one language key appears, check the html lang declaration in each input and verify the build directory. This fixture uses one declared language per page and checks index coverage. Use searches on the actual site to evaluate mixed-language pages and tokenization quality.

"},{"sha":"23f1282d3d640c4fed761f491a870b183765eb36","filename":"src/content/news/venture-briefing-date-from-workflow.md","status":"added","additions":27,"deletions":0,"changes":27,"blob_url":"https://github.com/yabby-groups/codex-venture/blob/635d85c0185d5d66c8e7c3747a401c6185515096/src%2Fcontent%2Fnews%2Fventure-briefing-date-from-workflow.md","raw_url":"https://github.com/yabby-groups/codex-venture/raw/635d85c0185d5d66c8e7c3747a401c6185515096/src%2Fcontent%2Fnews%2Fventure-briefing-date-from-workflow.md","contents_url":"https://api.github.com/repos/yabby-groups/codex-venture/contents/src%2Fcontent%2Fnews%2Fventure-briefing-date-from-workflow.md?ref=635d85c0185d5d66c8e7c3747a401c6185515096","patch":"@@ -0,0 +1,27 @@ +--- +titleZh: "让 CI 日期决定简报 URL" +titleEn: "Let the CI edition date determine the briefing URL" +summaryZh: "简报标题可以由模型起草，文件名可以在写入前由编辑批次的日期一次确定。" +summaryEn: "Let the model draft the headline and derive the filename from the edition date before writing." +type: "workflows" +category: "coding" +published: "2026-11-25T20:55:05+08:00" +verified: "2026-11-25" +version: "Commit 7ce66fc" +status: "current" +tested: false +tags: ["ai-practice"] +sources: [{"title": "Codex Venture 发布修复 / Publishing fix", "url": "https://github.com/yabby-groups/codex-venture/commit/7ce66fcd747541789aefd021111f4f43d0940f25"}] +--- + +

简报的文件名同时决定网址和归档位置。本站曾在发布端依赖编辑返回的 slug，模型填写的日期一旦与批次日期不一致，写入校验便会拒绝稿件。只改提示词仍要求模型每次都重现一个程序已经知道的值。

+ +

The briefing filename determines its URL and archive position. When the publishing job relied on the editor’s slug, a date that differed from the batch date caused the writer to reject the draft. A prompt fix would still ask the model to reproduce a value the program already knew.

+ +

本站的修复是在发布端核对批次时间，然后替换简报 slug。日报采用 YYYY-MM-DD，周报加 weekly- 前缀。写入函数继续校验日期和目标文件名，并拒绝覆盖已有稿件。这样即使模型返回错误日期，站点也会保留约定的归档 URL。

+ +

The fix checks the batch timestamp in the publishing job and replaces the briefing slug. Daily editions use YYYY-MM-DD, and weekly editions add the weekly- prefix. The writer still checks the date and destination and refuses to overwrite an existing file. The archive URL follows the publishing convention even if the model supplies the wrong date.

+ +

复用时，先在准备任务按编辑时区计算 edition_date，再将它随批次传到发布任务。用跨午夜的批次、带 weekly- 的批次和已有目标文件分别检查日期交接、前缀和重复发布。本文依据公开修复提交，未量化变更后的失败率。

+ +

To reuse the pattern, compute edition_date in the editorial timezone during preparation and carry it with the batch. Test a batch that crosses midnight, a weekly edition, and an existing destination to check the handoff, prefix, and repeat-publication behavior. This guide draws on the public fix. The post-change failure rate was not measured.

多个工作流如果从同一个 Git 分支恢复队列，可能以同一份旧状态开始处理。再各自写回时，后一次写入可能发生冲突。把更新同一队列的工作流放进同一个并发组，可以让 GitHub 一次只运行一项。

+ +

When several workflows restore a queue from the same Git branch, they can start from the same old state and conflict when they later write it back. Give workflows that update that queue the same concurrency group so GitHub runs them one at a time.

+ +

设置位置取决于共享状态的范围。如果准备、编辑和发布共同占用一次队列写入，应使用工作流级别的 concurrency。若只有一个 Job 写入，官方文档也支持 Job 级别的设置。下面示例适用于同一仓库里共享 editorial-state 分支的工作流。

+ +

Set concurrency at the scope that owns the shared state. Use workflow-level concurrency when preparation, editing, and publication together hold a queue write. GitHub also documents job-level concurrency if a single job owns the write. The example targets workflows in the same repository sharing an editorial-state branch.

+ +

默认设置只保留一个待运行项，后续等待项可以替换它。cancel-in-progress: false 保住正在运行的一项。若调度工作不能丢，按官方文档评估更多等待项的设置，或把到期任务保存在队列状态中，让后续触发重新领取。本文是官方文档整理，示例未在单独仓库执行。

+ +

The default keeps one pending run, which a newer pending run can replace. Setting cancel-in-progress to false protects the active run. If scheduled work must survive, evaluate the documented larger queue or persist due work so a later trigger can claim it. This guide is based on GitHub’s documentation, and the example was not run in a separate repository.

Codex Venture 增加可恢复的定时队列后，随新提交出现了一次 GitHub Actions 失败。准备 Job 的 checkout 配置写了两次 ref。一项是 main 分支，另一项引用了后续任务才会使用的准备结果。

+ +

After Codex Venture added a recoverable schedule, GitHub Actions recorded a failure at the new revision. The prepare job’s checkout configuration defined ref twice. One entry specified main and the other referred to an output intended for downstream jobs.

+ +
